transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-22
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (NexaHealth Head of ML), David Kim (NexaHealth Infra Lead), Sara Lopez (NexaHealth Security)

Summary: quick sync on onboarding, VPC and service account access, results from last week's benchmark, tuning suggestions, outstanding security/compliance items and next steps.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call. Priya and I from Redwood. Marta, David, Sara, you there?
[00:10] Marta Ruiz: Yep, here. Sorry for the slight delay, had another back-to-back.
[00:22] David Kim: Here. We're ready to go.
[00:30] Priya Patel: Great. So agenda - onboarding status, access setup, benchmarks, tuning, and security asks. We have about 45 minutes.
[01:05] Alex Chen: Last week we sent the VPC peering instructions and the service account template, and we also uploaded a small benchmark harness to the shared drive. Any updates on that?
[01:22] David Kim: We're partway through. I created the service account but hit a permission error when trying to create the peering - looks like our cloud team needs to approve. I'll open the ticket after this call.
[01:45] Sara Lopez: From security side, we reviewed the SOC2 summary you sent but need the encryption at rest keyflow documented. Specifically KMS key rotation and whether Redwood will have access.
[02:12] Priya Patel: Right, we can clarify. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys via our KMS integration, and we do not hold the plaintext keys. We'll send the full flow in the security pack.
[02:45] Marta Ruiz: Also, on the model side, the last runs showed some higher latency on long contexts. We ran 4k tokens and the 95th percentile spiked.
[03:05] Priya Patel: That's expected - sequence length impacts throughput. We recommended a quantized model variant for longer contexts; it reduced tokens/sec on our internal tests but improved cost. We can share the exact tuning we used.
[03:40] Alex Chen: Do you have the logs from the benchmark? We uploaded a spreadsheet with sample prompts and the harness link in the drive.
[03:58] Marta Ruiz: Yes, saw the sheet, but the team had trouble reproducing the exact seed. Might be a formatting issue in the CSV.
[04:20] Priya Patel: Ah, that happens - sometimes commas in the prompt cause row shifts. We added a helper script to normalize. I'll attach it to the deck.
[05:00] David Kim: Question on network - we're putting Redwood into a private subnet with NAT; will that affect the peering or the inbound egress rules?
[05:20] Alex Chen: For dedicated we ask for VPC peering; egress through NAT is fine for hosted flows but for Private deployment we prefer private peering so traffic doesn't traverse public internet. For the pilot you're doing private VPC peering.
[05:45] David Kim: Ok, we'll open that ticket. Any specific CIDR ranges we need to whitelist?
[06:10] Priya Patel: We sent the recommended CIDRs in the onboarding doc; I'll paste them in the chat again. Also note we need port 443 and the peering route table updates.
[06:35] Sara Lopez: On the compliance side, beyond SOC2, we need audit log retention options and RBAC role examples. Do you have a standard retention SLA?
[06:58] Alex Chen: Yes, we provide audit logs with configurable retention - default 90 days in the hosted offering; for Private we can extend per contract. We'll include the matrix in the security pack.
[07:20] Marta Ruiz: Great. Back to benchmarks - the 95th p slowed to 2.1s for 4k tokens on your hosted run. We saw 1.8s average in our on-prem tests with different sharding.
[07:45] Priya Patel: The delta could be due to batch configuration and KV cache warmup. If you can share request traces we can check whether the tokenization or prompt preamble is adding overhead.
[08:05] Marta Ruiz: We can do that. We'll redact PII and upload traces.
[08:30] Alex Chen: Also, a note on prompt caching - if you have repeated prefixes, enabling prefix caching gives a big speed up. We saw 20-30% improvement in similar workloads.
[08:50] David Kim: Do we need to change anything in the client to enable prefix caching?
[09:05] Priya Patel: No code changes for most SDKs; it's a routing flag on our side. We'll suggest config to set at route-level in the console.
[09:30] Sara Lopez: On the security flow for KMS - you mentioned customer-managed keys. Do you have a diagram showing key rotation and access control?
[09:55] Priya Patel: Not in the packet we shared; we'll add a diagram and detailed steps in the security pack.
[10:20] Alex Chen: Quick check - are we still aligned on success criteria for the pilot? Marta, you said 95th p latency under 2s for typical 2k-context prompts and hallucination rate below 1% for the NER job?
[10:40] Marta Ruiz: That's right. Also cost target was under $0.002 per 1k tokens processed for production-like throughput - though that's flexible for pilot.
[11:05] Priya Patel: Okay, we'll aim for that with a quantized variant and batching adjustments.
[11:30] David Kim: About data residency - our legal team asked where the inference logs live. Can logs be pushed to our S3 in-region?
[11:50] Alex Chen: For Private we can write logs to your S3 via a connector; for hosted we store logs in our region with export options. We'll include S3 sink options in the docs.
[12:20] Marta Ruiz: One wrinkle - one of our prompts triggered safety padding and trimmed output in a few cases. Is there a way to tune the moderation threshold or to get a safety log for false positives?
[12:45] Priya Patel: We can surface safety decisions in the audit logs and flag false positives. For model config, there's a moderation threshold setting we can adjust for the pilot to reduce overzealous blocking while keeping compliance.
[13:10] Alex Chen: Good. Next, on the action on your side - David, can you confirm service account role names? We need the exact roles so our bot can assume the permissions.
[13:28] David Kim: I'll confirm after the call, but likely a minimal set: compute admin for the peering and logging writer for the S3 sink.
[13:45] Priya Patel: That sounds minimal enough. We'll try the least privilege pattern first.
[14:05] Marta Ruiz: Any updates on costs? The estimate in the spreadsheet looked higher than expected for the 8k context runs.
[14:25] Alex Chen: Longer context increases token compute; switching to a model variant that uses sliding window attention or quantization can substantially reduce cost. Priya can share per-token cost numbers for each variant.
[14:45] Priya Patel: I have a small table - I'll export it. For example, quantized-16-bit variant shaved about 30% off cost in our tests at the expense of slightly higher latency for short contexts.
[15:10] David Kim: For the canary we want to test both variants and define rollback thresholds - e.g., latency increase >10% or error rate >1% triggers rollback.
[15:40] Alex Chen: Agreed. We'll propose a canary playbook with metrics and a traffic ramp schedule.
[16:05] Marta Ruiz: On instrumentation, we need token-level tracing for the NER pipeline, to analyze hallucinations. Is that something Redwood can emit?
[16:30] Priya Patel: Yes, we emit token-level timing and can correlate with model logits; the trace size is large but we can filter. We'll show how to sample traces.
[17:00] Sara Lopez: Make sure any traces that include PII are redacted. We'll provide a sanitizer spec.
[17:20] Alex Chen: Noted. We'll follow your sanitizer spec for uploads.
[17:40] David Kim: Logistics - when should we expect the SOC2 and KMS docs?
[17:55] Alex Chen: We'll push the security pack after this call - target EOD 2026-07-23, but I'll mark the action as due 2026-07-24 in case of follow ups.
[18:15] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. For the benchmark rerun, can you provide the exact Docker image and seed so we can reproduce locally?
[18:33] Priya Patel: Yes, benchmark repo includes Dockerfile and seed; I'll also attach a quick guide for reproducing on-prem vs hosted.
[18:55] Alex Chen: Okay next, any blockers we should know about?
[19:05] David Kim: Main blocker is the peering ticket and service account perms. Once that's resolved we can run the hosted canary.
[19:20] Marta Ruiz: From ML side, main blocker is the hallucination tuning; need to validate prompts and get logistic regression on false positives.
[19:40] Priya Patel: We'll help with prompt engineering and evaluation harness.
[20:00] Alex Chen: Great. Let's recap next steps at the end and assign owners.
[39:00] Alex Chen: (fast forward) to summarize - Redwood to deliver security pack (SOC2, KMS flow, audit log matrix), SE to share benchmark scripts and cost table, customer to set up peering and confirm roles, run benchmark and upload traces. We'll meet next week same time.
[39:30] Marta Ruiz: Confirmed. One more ask - can we get an anonymized sample of your audit logs format?
[39:55] Priya Patel: Yes, we'll redact and provide a sample.
[40:10] David Kim: I'll open the peering ticket and post the ticket ID to the thread.
[40:25] Sara Lopez: Thanks everyone.
[40:30] Alex Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with notes and the pack.

References:
- Shared drive: /redwood/nexahealth/pilot (benchmark harness, cost spreadsheet)
- Onboarding doc: link to VPC peering steps (see chat)

End of transcript
